newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodians seek food aid as flood toll hits 23.
newsitem.headline: Cambodians seek food aid as flood toll hits 23.

text.p: Hundreds of hungry villagers gathered in the Cambodian capital on Monday seeking handouts of food and cash from the government following floods that have killed at least 23 people.

Uy Samath, a senior official with the Cambodian Red Cross, said the death toll included seven drowned when a boat overturned on the rain-swollen Mekong River on Friday. Most of the victims were children or elderly people.

Hum Sophon, deputy director of the Cambodian Red Cross's disaster management department, said water levels remained serious downstream from Phnom Penh but were dropping in the capital and in provinces up river.

The government last week appealed to the international community for help. More than half a million people have been affected by the floods, with many made homeless. Thousands of hectares (acres) of crops have been submerged.
The United States, Japan, Britain and Australia have responded with aid pledges.
In the capital, hundreds of villagers were seen on Monday waiting for food and cash aid outside the palace of King Norodom Sihanouk and the residence of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

"We come here to ask for food from the king and prime ministers. We came here two days ago," Sun Thy, a 37-year-old farmer from neighbouring Kandal province, said outside Ranariddh's residence. "We are very hungry," he said.

Ta Suy, 66, said he and his family had come by boat from the hard-hit province of Kratie, some 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Phnom Penh, for relief aid to help offset the loss of their house and cattle.
Ranariddh was visiting flood victims in Kratie on Monday morning but a Red Cross official here said he had promised at the weekend to give food to the needy.
